articles.title: मध्य प्रदेश: उज्जैन में कैसा रहेगा मौसम? सुबह-शाम गुलाबी ठंड, दोपहर में तेज धूप; महाकाल भक्त ध्यान दें - Amar Ujala

मध्य प्रदेश: उज्जैन में कैसा रहेगा मौसम? सुबह-शाम गुलाबी ठंड, दोपहर में तेज धूप; महाकाल भक्त ध्यान दें
उज्जैन में मौसम का मिजाज इन दिनों बदल रहा है। सुबह और शाम हल्की ठंड महसूस हो रही है, जबकि दोपहर में अधिकतम तापमान 35 डिग्री तक पहुंच रहा है। जीवाजीराव वेधशाला के अधीक्षक डॉ. राजेंद्र प्रसाद गुप्त के अनुसार, दिसंबर और जनवरी में कड़ाके की ठंड पड़ने की संभावना रहती है।
विस्तार
बाबा महाकाल के दर्शन के लिए उज्जैन आने की योजना बना रहे हैं, तो मौसम के बदलते मिजाज को ध्यान में रखकर तैयारी करें। मध्य प्रदेश के उज्जैन में सुबह और शाम हल्की ठंड महसूस होने लगी है, लेकिन दोपहर में तेज धूप और गर्मी परेशान कर सकती है। जीवाजीराव वेधशाला के अधीक्षक डॉ. राजेंद्र प्रसाद गुप्त के मुताबिक, फिलहाल अधिकतम तापमान 35 डिग्री और रात का तापमान 19.5 डिग्री के आसपास है। ऐसे में भस्म आरती में शामिल होने वाले श्रद्धालुओं और दिन में महाकाल लोक घूमने की योजना बना रहे लोगों को कपड़ों और पानी का विशेष ध्यान रखना चाहिए।
सुबह-शाम ठंड, दोपहर में गर्मी से सामना
जीवाजीराव वेधशाला के अधीक्षक डॉ. राजेंद्र प्रसाद गुप्त के अनुसार, उज्जैन में अभी कड़ाके की ठंड शुरू नहीं हुई है, लेकिन सुबह और शाम हल्की ठंड का असर दिखाई देने लगा है। दूसरी ओर, दोपहर में अधिकतम तापमान 35 डिग्री तक पहुंचने से गर्मी महसूस हो रही है। रात का तापमान करीब 19.5 डिग्री दर्ज किया जा रहा है।
दिन और रात के तापमान में अंतर के कारण श्रद्धालुओं को दर्शन के समय के अनुसार अपनी तैयारी करनी चाहिए। सुबह जल्दी मंदिर पहुंचने वालों को हल्के गर्म कपड़े रखने चाहिए, जबकि दोपहर में बाहर घूमने वालों को तेज धूप से बचाव करना जरूरी है।
कब बढ़ेगी उज्जैन में ठंड?
डॉ. गुप्त के अनुसार, ठंड बढ़ने का संबंध केवल बारिश से नहीं है। पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में होने वाली बर्फबारी और सूर्य की किरणों की स्थिति सहित कई मौसमी कारक तापमान को प्रभावित करते हैं। पृथ्वी की सूर्य के सापेक्ष स्थिति में बदलाव के साथ सूर्य की किरणें सर्दियों में अपेक्षाकृत तिरछी पड़ती हैं, जिससे धरती को मिलने वाली ऊर्जा में कमी आती है और तापमान घटने लगता है।
दिसंबर-जनवरी में महसूस होगी कड़ाके की ठंड
वेधशाला अधीक्षक के मुताबिक, उज्जैन में कड़ाके की ठंड के लिए अभी इंतजार करना होगा। दिसंबर और जनवरी में आमतौर पर ठंड का असर अधिक महसूस होता है। हालांकि, वास्तविक तापमान और ठंड की तीव्रता उस समय की मौसम परिस्थितियों पर निर्भर करेगी।
महाकाल दर्शन करने वालों के लिए 5 जरूरी टिप्स
भस्म आरती के समय गर्म कपड़े रखें: सुबह 4 बजे की भस्म आरती में शामिल होने जा रहे हैं, तो हल्का स्वेटर या शॉल साथ रखें।
दोपहर में धूप से बचाव करें: दिन में दर्शन या भ्रमण के दौरान टोपी, पानी की बोतल और गमछा साथ रखें।
बच्चों और बुजुर्गों का ध्यान रखें: तापमान में उतार-चढ़ाव के कारण छोटे बच्चों और बुजुर्गों के कपड़ों का विशेष ध्यान रखें।
महाकाल लोक घूमने की योजना बनाएं: शाम के समय घूमना सुविधाजनक हो सकता है, लेकिन मौसम के अनुसार हल्के गर्म कपड़े साथ रखें।
बदलते मौसम के लिए तैयार रहें: सर्दी-जुकाम से बचाव के लिए जरूरत के मुताबिक गर्म कपड़े बैग में रखें और पर्याप्त पानी पीते रहें।
महाकाल दर्शन के लिए उज्जैन आने वाले श्रद्धालुओं के लिए फिलहाल सबसे जरूरी बात यही है कि सुबह-शाम की हल्की ठंड और दोपहर की गर्मी, दोनों को ध्यान में रखकर यात्रा की तैयारी करें।

Hyderabad: Cybercrime police registered a case after a mobile phone was found hidden in a women’s washroom at a public sector company’s office in Secunderabad.
According to police, a 35-year-old chief manager went to the sixth-floor washroom at about 10.30 am on Oct 13. Under the washbasin, directly opposite the commode, she noticed a small object wrapped in white paper with two holes in it.
“She initially thought it was a room freshener, but on picking it up, she found it was a mobile phone stuck to the wall with double-sided tape,” a cybercrime police officer said.
She then took the phone out of the washroom and casually asked the floor’s office attendant who it belonged to. The complainant told police that the attendant snatched the phone and ran off. She immediately alerted colleagues, the HR department and main-gate security personnel, following which the suspect was caught.
“When staff tried to check the phone, they found a folder locked with a PIN. When the attendant was asked to enter the PIN, he grabbed the phone and threw it to the ground,” the complainant alleged.
Suspecting the accused may have kept the phone in the washroom for a long time to secretly record videos, the complainant asked the police to take strict legal action against the attendant and anyone else involved.
Police were also requested to retrieve the content from the device and protect the privacy of the women affected.
The complaint was first registered at Gandhi Nagar police station on Oct 13 under Sections 77 (voyeurism) and 238 (causing disappearance of evidence or giving false information to screen an offender) of the BNS and Section 66E of the Information Technology Act. On the instructions of senior officers, it was transferred to Hyderabad cybercrime police on Oct 22 and re-registered.
“The accused was arrested and is currently in judicial remand. We have moved a petition seeking his custody to find out more details. Once the court grants custody, cybercrime police will interrogate him. No videos were found on the device, but forensic analysis may provide more details,” a Gandhi Nagar police officer said.

Maharashtra heatwave: Amravati records state’s highest temperature at 37.4 degrees Celsius, Mumbai touches 37
Mumbai City recorded a maximum temperature of 37 degrees Celsius, 3.3 degrees above normal, while the Santacruz observatory (representative of the suburbs) registered 37.1 degrees Celsius, 2.9 degrees above normal. The city also continued to experience warm nights
Mumbai’s minimum temperature stood at 27.4 degrees Celsius, 2.7 degrees above normal. (Pic/ Ashish Raje)
Maharashtra continued to experience hot and dry weather on Friday, with temperatures above normal in several parts of the state. Amravati recorded the highest maximum temperature at 37.4 degrees Celsius, 5.1 degrees above normal, while Mumbai recorded 37 degrees Celsius.
Gondia reported the lowest minimum temperature in the state at 17 degrees Celsius, according to the India Meteorological Department’s (IMD) daily weather report.

Schools and other learning institutions have been urged to implement immediate measures to protect learners and staff following a heatwave alert issued by the Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services (DCCMS).
The Department has forecast temperatures of up to 42C in parts of the Southern Region, with unusually high temperatures also expected across the Central, Northern and lakeshore areas.
In a statement, Secretary for Education Dr Ken Ndala said institutions should strictly adhere to precautionary measures aimed at safeguarding learners, teachers and support staff while maintaining continuity in education.
Schools have been advised to adjust timetables, relax uniform requirements and adopt flexible learning arrangements where necessary to reduce exposure to extreme heat.
Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines
The ministry has also directed institutions to suspend or reschedule outdoor activities, including sports, assemblies, parades and manual work, during the hottest part of the day, between 10am and 3pm.
Additional guidance includes ensuring continuous access to safe drinking water, encouraging regular hydration, keeping classrooms cool and well-ventilated, making use of shaded areas and avoiding overcrowding.
Schools have also been asked to pay particular attention to vulnerable groups, including young children, people with albinism, pregnant members of staff and those living with chronic health conditions.
"The ministry also reminds institutions to make use of the El Niño Practical Guidance for the Education Sector 2026-2027 booklets that have been distributed to strengthen preparedness and response to climate-related hazards," the statement said.
The advisory forms part of wider efforts to minimise the impact of extreme weather conditions on learning and to reduce health risks associated with prolonged exposure to high temperatures.

articles.full_text:
New Delhi [India], October 23 (ANI): GIFT Nifty has achieved a new milestone by recording an all-time high open interest of 4,78,079 contracts valued at USD 21.74 billion on October 22, 2026, reflecting growing participation in derivatives trading at India's International Financial Services Centre (IFSC).
According to a press release issued by NSE International Exchange (NSEIX) on Friday, the latest milestone marks another significant achievement for GIFT Nifty, which has emerged as an important benchmark linked to the Indian equity market.
The exchange highlighted that trading activity on NSEIX has witnessed substantial growth since the commencement of full-scale GIFT Nifty operations on July 3, 2023.
Since the launch of full-scale operations, GIFT Nifty has recorded a cumulative trading volume exceeding 78.12 million contracts, with total cumulative turnover reaching USD 3.61 trillion as of October 22, 2026.
The figures highlight the expansion of trading activity on the platform over the past three years, alongside growing participation in India-linked derivatives through the international financial services ecosystem.
Expressing satisfaction over the milestone, NSEIX acknowledged the contribution of market participants towards the growth and success of GIFT Nifty.
"We are glad to witness the success of GIFT Nifty and express our sincere gratitude to all the participants for their overwhelming support and for making GIFT Nifty a successful contract," the exchange stated.
NSEIX, an international multi-asset exchange established at GIFT City on June 5, 2017, operates under the regulatory oversight of the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA).
The exchange offers a diversified portfolio of financial products, including Indian single-stock derivatives, index derivatives, currency derivatives, depository receipts and global stocks.
It also provides primary market products such as equity share listings, Special Purpose Acquisition Companies (SPACs), Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs), debt securities and environmental, social and governance (ESG) debt securities. (ANI)

IMD sounds yellow alert for Chandigarh Tricity as thunderstorm, gusty winds likely on Saturday
Panchkula records lowest day and night temperatures in Haryana and Tricity; weekend showers possible before dry spell on Monday and Tuesday
Residents of Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula should brace for a spell of unsettled weather over the weekend, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) sounding a yellow alert for thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds of 30-40 kmph on Saturday. Isolated showers are likely across the region on Saturday and Sunday, while the weather is expected to turn dry on Monday and Tuesday before scattered showers return at isolated places from Wednesday.
Panchkula remained the coolest station in the Tricity and Haryana on Friday, recording a maximum temperature of 28.9°C and a minimum of 13.7°C. Its maximum was also the lowest reported in Punjab and Haryana, while its night temperature was just 0.1°C higher than the 13.6°C recorded at Pathankot, which registered the lowest minimum in the two states.
Temperatures continued to dip across the Tricity. Chandigarh recorded a maximum of 31.4°C, down 0.2°C from Thursday, while the minimum also fell 0.2°C to 14.8°C. Both readings remained marginally above normal, by 1.5°C and 0.1°C, respectively.
Mohali recorded a maximum of 30.6°C, with no change from the previous day, while its minimum fell 1.1°C to 16.7°C.
The region remained dry on Friday, with no rainfall recorded in Chandigarh, Mohali or Panchkula. Relative humidity in Chandigarh remained high, with the maximum at 85 per cent and minimum at 36 per cent, although the maximum was lower than the previous day’s 92 per cent.
The IMD forecast indicates isolated rainfall in Punjab on Saturday and Sunday, with the same outlook for Haryana and Chandigarh on Sunday; Haryana and Chandigarh are forecast to remain dry on Saturday despite the thunderstorm and gusty-wind warning. The alert is confined to Saturday, with no warning listed for the following days.
After the weekend, dry weather is forecast for Monday and Tuesday. Isolated showers may return on Wednesday and Thursday in parts of Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh, according to the seven-day outlook.
